skill.name: remotion-render
skill.description: Render React and Remotion TSX components to MP4 through the inference.sh CLI with configurable dimensions, FPS, duration, codec, and props.
skill.summary: Turn Remotion component code into configurable MP4 videos through inference.sh.
skill.author: infsh-skills

security_audit.summary: Static command findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences, inline backticks, and documentation examples. Hardcoded URL findings are documentation or media links, but the skill still sends user-supplied Remotion code to an external inference.sh renderer and grants broad belt CLI access.

remediation.issue: Submitted TSX and props leave the local environment for rendering.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear privacy notice before use and advise users not to submit secrets, private source code, or sensitive asset URLs.
Restrict the allowed command pattern to the minimum belt login and belt app run operations required for rendering.

remediation.issue: The examples do not describe validation expectations for remote rendering input.
remediation.suggestion: Document supported imports, asset handling, and expected failure modes so users avoid unsafe or unsupported component code.

content.value_statement: Teams need repeatable video renders without opening a manual editor. This skill sends Remotion TSX to inference.sh and returns a configurable MP4 render.
actual_capabilities: Renders a default exported Remotion component to MP4 through the inference.sh CLI.
Accepts configurable width, height, FPS, duration, composition ID, props, and codec settings.
Uses documented Remotion APIs such as AbsoluteFill, Sequence, spring, interpolate, Audio, Video, and Img.
Supports command-line examples through belt app run for quick rendering workflows.
Shows Python SDK usage for normal runs and streaming progress updates.
limitations: Requires an inference.sh account, the belt CLI, and network access.
Submitted code and props are processed by an external rendering service.
The component must export a valid default Remotion component.
It does not provide a full video editor or timeline authoring interface.

use_cases.title: Automated Launch Videos
use_cases.description: Create short product announcements from reusable Remotion components and campaign-specific props.

use_cases.title: Data-Driven Motion Graphics
use_cases.description: Render counters, charts, and status visuals from generated React component instructions.

use_cases.title: Developer Video Prototypes
use_cases.description: Test Remotion animation ideas quickly before moving them into a production video pipeline.

prompt_templates.title: Render a Simple Title Card
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a three second Remotion title card with centered text, a dark background, 30 FPS, and 1080p output.

prompt_templates.title: Render with Props
prompt_templates.prompt: Render a Remotion component that accepts title, subtitle, and brand color props for a five second announcement video.

prompt_templates.title: Render a Sequenced Animation
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a four step Remotion sequence with staggered text, smooth fades, and a square 1080 by 1080 output.

prompt_templates.title: Render a Production Variant
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Remotion render with explicit FPS, duration, codec, resolution, props, and notes about any external assets used.

output_examples.input: Create a five second product teaser with a title, subtitle, and soft fade-in.
output_examples.output: The skill returns an MP4 render link for a 1080p video with the requested title animation and timing.

output_examples.input: Render a square animated counter for a social post.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a square MP4 with a numeric progress animation, configured duration, and requested frame rate.

output_examples.input: Generate a Remotion render using provided campaign props.
output_examples.output: The skill renders the component with the supplied values and reports the resulting video location.

best_practices: Keep component code small, deterministic, and focused on one renderable composition.
Use props for repeated values so variants can be rendered without rewriting the component.
Review code and assets before submission because rendering happens through an external service.
anti_patterns: Do not include secrets, private tokens, or confidential source code in submitted props or TSX.
Do not rely on unsupported imports outside React and Remotion without verifying service support.
Do not use this as a replacement for reviewing video output before publication.

faq.question: What does this skill render?
faq.answer: It renders React and Remotion component code into MP4 videos through the inference.sh rendering app.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it need a local Remotion setup?
faq.answer: The documented workflow uses the belt CLI and inference.sh service instead of a local Remotion render pipeline.

faq.question: Can I pass custom values into the render?
faq.answer: Yes. The input schema supports props, composition ID, width, height, FPS, duration, and codec settings.

faq.question: Is submitted code processed locally?
faq.answer: No. The examples send code to the infsh/remotion-render app through inference.sh for remote rendering.

faq.question: What should I avoid submitting?
faq.answer: Avoid secrets, private tokens, proprietary source code, and sensitive asset URLs unless your policy allows external processing.
